EAN-13 Encoding

ArithmeticDivisibilityNumber Theory
Game: A shop barcode is a thirteen-digit number drawn as bars; the last digit is worked out from the others. There is nothing to win or lose.
How to play: Press one of the first twelve digits to raise it by one, or select it and type a new digit, and watch the last digit and the bars change.

Look for the math

The EAN-13 code on a shop item is thirteen digits. The last is a check digit: it is chosen so that a little sum comes out a multiple of ten.

The check digit

Write the digits d1 d2 … d13. Then d1 + 3d2 + d3 + 3d4 + … + d11 + 3d12 + d13 ≡ 0 (mod 10), so the last digit is whatever makes the sum a multiple of ten. The logic test checked this on more than half a million codes, with every digit value in every position. Because 1 and 3 are coprime to 10, changing any one digit changes the sum by a non-multiple of ten, so every single wrong digit is caught; the test tried every wrong digit in every position of 2,000 codes. Swapping two neighbours a, b changes the sum by ±2(a − b), which is a multiple of ten only when a and b differ by 5: the test found exactly those swaps go unnoticed.

UPC-A and ISBN

A twelve-digit UPC-A code is an EAN-13 with a 0 in front, and the check digit stays the same because the weights line up: the test confirmed it for 50,000 codes. A book’s ISBN-10 becomes an EAN-13 by putting 978 in front of its first nine digits and working out a new check digit: 0-14-200057-4 becomes 9780142000571, as on the page.

The bars

The code is 95 modules wide: guard bars at each end and in the middle, and seven modules for each of twelve digits. The first digit has no bars of its own. It picks, for each of the six left digits, one of two patterns (L, odd, or G, even), so that the scanner can tell the code is not upside down and can recover the first digit. The test turned the bars of 200,000 random codes back into digits without a mistake.

Type 978 at the start of the code, then six more digits of any book’s ISBN, and compare the last digit with the book’s own.
